MUQATIL:18:20-21/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:20-21/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:20-21/r4.claim: God reveals the youths to disbelievers so they know the resurrection promise is true and the Hour is coming without doubt.

MUQATIL:18:20-21/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:20-21/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:20-21/r5.claim: The Hour is certain and imminent; lā rayba means there is no doubt it will occur.

MUQATIL:18:20-21/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:20-21/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:20-21/r6.claim: People disputed what to do: some proposed a building, while the believers who prevailed built a mosque at the cave entrance.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p175#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p175#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p175#2/r3.claim: Qatāda says God brought the sleepers to the notice of people of the later age, not by resurrecting them at the final Resurrection.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p175#2/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p175#2/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p175#2/r4.claim: The later community disputed bodily resurrection: believers, including their king, affirmed bodies and souls would rise, while the People of the Book said souls rise without bodies; the sleepers became proof for bodily resurrection.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p175#2/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p175#2/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p175#2/r5.claim: A sleeper's old coins were recognized in the Roman city of Fasus; the townspeople thought he had found a treasure, and disclosure led the king to affirm bodily resurrection.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p177/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p177/r1.speaker: عكرمة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p177/r1.claim: ʿIkrima's account, transmitted by Qatāda, says Roman princes became Muslims and fled their people; after their generation passed, a Muslim community disputed whether bodies or only souls return.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p177/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p177/r2.speaker: عكرمة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p177/r2.claim: In the account, a distressed king prayed for a sign; the sleepers' messenger was sent for food, recognized the changed city and manifest faith, and was brought before the king.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p177/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p177/r3.speaker: عكرمة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p177/r3.claim: The king gathers the people and declares that God has sent a sign proving people will be raised with their bodies; when the youths see one another, God causes them to die.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p177/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p177/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p177/r4.claim: When the returned youth and his companions meet, they die because their appointed lifetimes have now run out.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p178/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p178/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p178/r1.claim: The group with authority were the kings and nobles, who decided to build a mosque over the sleepers.

FARRA:v2p137/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p137/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p137/r5.claim: أعثرنا عليهم means We made them known or brought them to light; the same verb in 5:107 means discovered.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p265#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p265#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p265#3/r1.claim: Aʿtharnā means We revealed or informed them; the idiom “I never found so-and-so doing harm” uses the same root.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p265#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p265#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p265#3/r2.claim: Those who prevailed over the matter means the leaders and people whose authority was obeyed.

TUSTARI:18:21/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:18:21/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:18:21/r1.claim: The outward meaning is political authority; inwardly, it is the spirit, the intellect’s understanding, and the heart’s alertness through remembrance of God.

TAB-FULL:v15p161/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p161/r6.speaker: عمرو
TAB-FULL:v15p161/r6.claim: When the envoy returned to the cave with the people, God caused the youths to sleep again, and the people proposed building a place of worship over them.

TAB-FULL:v15p197/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p197/r3.speaker: وهب بن منبه
TAB-FULL:v15p197/r3.claim: When the messenger led the king and people to the cave, terror kept them from entering; they later built a church or mosque there for prayer.

TAB-FULL:v15p208/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p208/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p208/r1.claim: When Yamlīkha delayed, his companions feared Daqyanus had captured him; hearing horses, they prayed, exchanged farewells, and expected to face the tyrant.

TAB-FULL:v15p208/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p208/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p208/r2.claim: They found Areus and the townspeople at the cave instead; Yamlīkha told the youths what happened, and they understood God had awakened them as a sign of resurrection.

TAB-FULL:v15p208/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p208/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p208/r3.claim: A sealed copper chest held lead tablets naming the youths and saying they fled Daqyanus to protect their faith; the king had sealed their cave with stones.

TAB-FULL:v15p208/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p208/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p208/r4.claim: After reading the tablets, the townspeople praised God for showing them a sign of resurrection and found the youths alive-looking, unchanged, and seated in the cave.

TAB-FULL:v15p208/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p208/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p208/r5.claim: The righteous king Theodosius came, embraced and wept over the youths, who welcomed him and then returned to their resting places and died.

TAB-FULL:v15p208/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p208/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p208/r6.claim: The king first ordered gold coffins, but after the youths asked in a dream to remain on earth, he placed them in teak; fear then barred entry, and their cave became a mosque and annual festival site.

TAB-FULL:v15p211/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p211/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عبيد بن عمير
TAB-FULL:v15p211/r1.claim: The youths were raised under a Muslim king, hungry; one judged they had slept a day or less, then deferred the true duration to God and went to buy food with old coins.

TAB-FULL:v15p211/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p211/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن عبيد بن عمير
TAB-FULL:v15p211/r3.claim: Pagans claimed the youths as their ancestors and proposed a building for worship; Muslims claimed them as fellow believers and proposed a mosque for prayer.

TAB-FULL:v15p211/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p211/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p211/r4.claim: God raised the youths so they would question one another, then exposed them to doubters as proof that He can raise the dead, as the verse itself explains.

TAB-FULL:v15p216#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p216#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p216#2/r1.claim: The disputants were Theodosius’s people debating whether God recreates His servants after death and decay.

TAB-FULL:v15p216#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p216#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p216#2/r2.claim: Those finding the sleepers proposed building over them, saying their Lord knew their circumstances; the people who prevailed then resolved to make a mosque there.

TAB-FULL:v15p216#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p216#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p216#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies those who prevailed and proposed the mosque as the youths’ enemies.

TAB-FULL:v15p216#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p216#2/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن عبيد بن عمير
TAB-FULL:v15p216#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr’s account distinguishes pagans who wanted a building and worship from Muslims who wanted a mosque for prayer.

TAB-FULL:v15p216/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p216/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p216/r1.claim: As God revived the youths in their former appearance so they could question one another, He disclosed them to doubters so they would recognize His power to raise the dead and the certainty of the Hour.

TAB-FULL:v15p216/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p216/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p216/r2.claim: Qatāda says God revealed the youths to those who denied the account, so they would know the promise and the Hour are real.

ZAJJAJ:v3p276/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p276/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p276/r4.claim: God disclosed them so deniers of resurrection would know the promise is true and believers grow in faith; إذ may attach to أعثرنا or ليعلموا.

ZAJJAJ:v3p277/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p277/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p277/r1.claim: The believers prevailed after the youths were discovered; their proposal to build a mosque indicates belief in resurrection.

NAHHAS:v2p451/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p451/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p451/r13.claim: ‘When they disputed among themselves’ is a time adverb governed by ‘so they might know,’ referring to when God raised the youths.

SULAMI:v1p408#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p408#2/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p408#2/r1.claim: God showed the cave youths wondrous works, made them witnesses to His might, and gave them the station described by the address to the Prophet about fleeing from them.

THALABI:v6p151/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p151/r3.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
THALABI:v6p151/r3.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Theodosius ruled 38 years as people split over bodily resurrection; as deniers gained influence, he prayed in sackcloth and ashes for a clarifying sign.

THALABI:v6p151/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p151/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p151/r4.claim: God intends to reveal the cave youths to vindicate Theodosius's faith and make their revival a sign that the Hour and resurrection are real.

THALABI:v6p155/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p155/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p155/r2.claim: After hearing Tamlikha, the youths realize God had kept them asleep for the whole period so their awakening could affirm resurrection and the coming Hour.

THALABI:v6p155/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p155/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p155/r3.claim: Armos opens the sealed lead record, which identifies the seven youths and explains that Daqyanus sealed them in the cave for refusing to abandon faith.

THALABI:v6p155/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p155/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p155/r4.claim: The townspeople praise God for showing them a sign of resurrection and find the youths seated, radiant, and with clothing unspoiled.

THALABI:v6p156/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p156/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p156/r1.claim: Armos and the townspeople urgently summon Theodosius to witness the youths as a sign of resurrection; the king rises relieved and thanks God for preserving the faith inherited from his forebears.

THALABI:v6p156/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p156/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p156/r2.claim: The king and the townspeople travel to the cave, where the youths rejoice, prostrate, greet him, and commend his rule to God's protection.

THALABI:v6p156/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p156/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p156/r3.claim: The youths bid the king farewell and ask God to preserve him and protect him from the harm of jinn and people.

THALABI:v6p156/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p156/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p156/r4.claim: As the king stands, God takes the youths' lives again; after they reject golden coffins in a dream, he orders a teak coffin and they remain hidden by terror.

THALABI:v6p156/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p156/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p156/r5.claim: The king orders a mosque built at the cave entrance and establishes a major annual feast for the youths.

THALABI:v6p156/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p156/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p156/r6.claim: A variant says Tamlikha enters alone to reassure the youths; God takes their lives, conceals their location, and no one can find them.

THALABI:v6p161#2/r19.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p161#2/r19.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p161#2/r19.claim: Atharna means that God made the townspeople discover or learn about the youths; the verb can mean to discover something or make another discover it.

THALABI:v6p161#2/r20.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p161#2/r20.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p161#2/r20.claim: Ibn Abbas says the townspeople disputed whether to build a structure or a mosque over the youths; Muslims wanted a mosque because the youths shared their faith.

THALABI:v6p161#2/r21.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p161#2/r21.speaker: عكرمة
THALABI:v6p161#2/r21.claim: Ikrima says the dispute concerned bodily resurrection: Muslims affirmed resurrection of body and soul, while others claimed only souls return; the youths' revival demonstrated the former.

THALABI:v6p161#2/r22.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p161#2/r22.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p161#2/r22.claim: Other reported disputes concerned how long the youths stayed or how many they were.

THALABI:v6p161#2/r23.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p161#2/r23.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p161#2/r23.claim: Those who prevailed and proposed a mosque are identified either as Theodosius and his companions or, in another view, the believers; the latter returns to the first account.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p295/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p295/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p295/r1.claim: أعثرنا عليهم may mean that God disclosed the youths to their townspeople.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p295/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p295/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p295/r2.claim: Alternatively, it means God brought the townspeople to discover them through His mercy.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p295/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p295/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p295/r3.claim: Their discovery lets the townspeople know the resurrection promise is true: the One who raised people after a sleep like death can raise the dead from their graves.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p295/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p295/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p295/r4.claim: Alternatively, the cave youths themselves come to see the truth of God's promise of their own resurrection.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p295/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p295/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p295/r5.claim: After their messenger's old coin and unfamiliar appearance caused alarm, a righteous king recognized him as possibly one of the youths from the time of Decianus; after questioning him, the king and people went to the cave, the youths heard the crowd, feared for their faith, and God caused them to die a true death.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p295/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p295/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p295/r6.claim: One disagreement was whether the youths were alive or dead.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p295/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p295/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p295/r7.claim: Alternatively, once their death was known, people disputed whether to build a marker over them or a mosque.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p295/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p295/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p295/r8.claim: One account says the king planned to bury them in a gold coffin, but a visitor in a dream said they were created from earth and should be left to return to it.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p570/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p570/r1.speaker: العلماء بأخبار القدماء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p570/r1.claim: Daqyanus sealed the cave, intending the youths to die of thirst and hunger there; two believers recorded their names, lineage, and story on lead inside a copper chest by the entrance for future believers to discover.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p570/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p570/r2.speaker: العلماء بأخبار القدماء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p570/r2.claim: Many generations later, the righteous king Tindusis faced a dispute about the Resurrection and prayed for a sign; God inspired a man to dismantle the cave entrance while building a sheep enclosure.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p570/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p570/r3.speaker: العلماء بأخبار القدماء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p570/r3.claim: God terror kept people from entering; the youths awoke after more than three hundred years, sent a companion for food, were discovered, and the king came with the townspeople to see them.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p570/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p570/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p570/r4.claim: The phrase means God made the youths known and revealed them; the commentary also discusses the verb earlier in al-Maʾida.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p571/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p571/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p571/r1.claim: The discovery lets the king and his subjects know that resurrection, reward, punishment, and the Hour are certain.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p571/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p571/r2.speaker: عكرمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p571/r2.claim: The dispute among the people of that age concerned resurrection; al-Wahidi calls this the likeliest interpretation.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p571/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p571/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p571/r3.claim: Their disputed matter was resurrection; the time clause is governed by “We made them known,” meaning God disclosed them as the dispute arose.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p571/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p571/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p571/r4.claim: Alternatively, the time clause can depend on “so that they know”: they learned at the time of their dispute.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p571/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p571/r5.speaker: ابن عباس رواية عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p571/r5.claim: A man sent to buy food showed the youths a coin bearing Decianus's image, and they disputed with him and rejected his account.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p571/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p571/r6.speaker: قوم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p571/r6.claim: Some say the dispute concerned how long the youths had stayed, but al-Wahidi says this does not fit the clause's syntax unless it is detached as a new command to recall the dispute.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p571/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p571/r7.speaker: قوم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p571/r7.claim: Some say they disputed their number; al-Wahidi rejects this for the same syntactic reason as the proposed dispute about their duration.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p571/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p571/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p571/r8.claim: Another reported view is that the dispute concerned building over the youths and making a mosque; the surrounding words about building support it.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p571/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p571/r9.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p571/r9.claim: The proposed building was meant to conceal the youths from people.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p573/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p573/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p573/r1.claim: “Their Lord knows best about them” suggests a dispute over their number, and means that God knows their count; compare the next verse.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p573/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p573/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p573/r2.claim: The phrase “their Lord knows best” may be God's own new statement or the words of people arguing about the youths' number.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p573/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p573/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p573/r3.claim: Those who prevailed in the matter were believers who did not doubt resurrection.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p573/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p573/r4.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p573/r4.claim: Exegetes identify those who prevailed as King Theodosius and his companions.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p573/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p573/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p573/r5.claim: The mosque indicates that believers in resurrection prevailed, since mosques belong to believers.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p573/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p573/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p573/r6.claim: “Over them” means placing the structure behind or around them, as when a wall is built around something.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p573/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p573/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p573/r7.claim: The account says the king built a mosque at the cave entrance and established an annual festival there.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p573/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p573/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p573/r8.claim: Al-Wahidi says the verse is difficult in its apparent wording and arrangement, and that God knows best what it means.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:20-21/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:20-21/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:20-21/r2.claim: God made the townspeople discover them so the people of that time would know God's promise of reward and punishment is true and that resurrection is certain.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:20-21/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:20-21/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:20-21/r3.claim: The discovery let people use the youths' story as evidence that resurrection is true.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:20-21/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:20-21/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:20-21/r4.claim: The contemporaries disputed the youths' duration and number; another reported account says believers wanted a mosque while unbelievers wanted a wall around them.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:20-21/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:20-21/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:20-21/r5.claim: The phrase “their Lord knows them best” indicates a dispute about their number; the believers prevailed and built a mosque at the cave entrance.

JISHUMI:v6p4382/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4382/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4382/r1.claim: Their escape shows that they fled to preserve their religion and took every precaution for it, urging people to follow their example.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p160#3/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p160#3/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p160#3/r3.claim: Aʿtharnā means God made people discover them; this showed Bidrus's people, who denied resurrection, that God's promise and the Hour are true.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p160#3/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p160#3/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p160#3/r4.claim: He says the dispute concerned building over them: Muslims proposed a place of prayer because they shared the sleepers' religion, while polytheists preferred a structure because of kinship.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p160#3/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p160#3/r5.speaker: عكرمة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p160#3/r5.claim: He says they disputed whether resurrection restores bodies and souls together or only souls; raising the sleepers demonstrated both return.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p160#3/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p160#3/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p160#3/r6.claim: Other views say the dispute concerned how long the sleepers remained or how many they were.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p161/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p161/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p161/r1.claim: Those who prevailed were King Bidrus and his companions, who resolved to build a mosque over the sleepers.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p665/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p665/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p665/r1.claim: As with their sleep and awakening, God disclosed them for a purpose: to show that the promised resurrection is true, since their experience parallels death and revival.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p665/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p665/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p665/r10.claim: God inspired a shepherd to open the cave mouth for a sheepfold; the envoy’s old coin led to suspicion of treasure, and his account brought the king and townspeople to witness the sign of resurrection.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p665/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p665/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p665/r11.claim: The youths commended the king to God’s protection, returned to their beds, and died; the king changed their gold coffins to teak after seeing in a dream that they disliked gold, then built a mosque.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p665/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p665/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p665/r12.claim: “Their Lord knows best” may be the disputants conceding that they cannot establish the youths’ lineage, circumstances, or duration.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p665/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p665/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p665/r13.claim: Alternatively, it is God’s rebuttal of speculators, either the contemporaneous disputants or the People of the Book who disputed the story in the Prophet’s time.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p665/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p665/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p665/r2.claim: “When they dispute” attaches to God’s disclosure: disputants differed over whether resurrection restores souls alone or bodies with souls; the youths’ case proves bodies return alive and sentient.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p665/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p665/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p665/r3.claim: An alternative reading of the dispute is that people discussed the youths’ story and the sign God showed through them.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p665/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p665/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p665/r4.claim: Another alternative is that, after the youths died, people debated how to hide their place and block access to the cave.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p665/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p665/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p665/r5.claim: Building over the cave entrance would keep people from approaching their resting place, as an enclosure protected the Prophet’s grave.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p665/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p665/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p665/r6.claim: Those who prevailed were the Muslims and their king, who had the stronger claim to the youths and the building.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p665/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p665/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p665/r7.claim: They built a mosque at the cave entrance so Muslims could pray there and seek blessing from the youths’ location.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p665/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p665/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p665/r8.claim: The narrative says Daqyanus forced noble youths to worship idols; they fled, and a dog either spoke of loving God’s beloved and offered to guard them or followed them with its shepherd owner, who shared their faith.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p665/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p665/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p665/r9.claim: Before their awakening, a righteous believing man ruled the city while its people disputed resurrection; he withdrew in sackcloth and ashes and asked God to disclose the truth.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p506#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p506#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p506#2/r1.claim: 'Likewise' links discovering the youths to the prior awakening; athara is the causative of stumbling on something, a metaphor for discovering concealed knowledge.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p506#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p506#2/r2.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p506#2/r2.claim: Al-Tabari says 'so that they might know' refers to the Muslim community of the youths' era, which had fallen into dispute over bodily resurrection; God revealed the sleepers, convincing doubters and consoling a distressed king.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p506#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p506#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p506#2/r3.claim: On al-Tabari's reading, the king was so troubled by people's doubt that he wore rough garments, sat in ashes, and prayed for proof until the youths were discovered.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p506#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p506#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p506#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, 'so that they might know' refers to the youths themselves, whose story became a sign of bodily resurrection.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p506#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p506#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p506#2/r5.claim: The phrase 'the Hour has no doubt in it' asserts that the Hour is objectively certain even though people may doubt it.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p506#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p506#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p506#2/r6.claim: A separate disagreement concerns whether to cover the cave or build over it; some said the youths were dead and others alive, and a dominant party proposed a mosque. Qatada identifies that party as the rulers.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p506#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p506#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p506#2/r7.claim: One account says believers who wanted the cave obscured prevailed over those who insisted on construction, and made the required building a mosque.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p506#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p506#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p506#2/r8.claim: Another account says unbelievers wanted a church or pagan shrine, but believers resisted and insisted on a mosque.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p506#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p506#2/r9.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p506#2/r9.claim: Ubayd ibn Umayr says God concealed the youths' trace from people, prompting construction of a building to mark their location.

TABRISI:18:21-22/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:21-22/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:18:21-22/r1.claim: An alternative account places the dispute after the ruler and people entered the cave and the youths fell dead; some proposed a tomb-like building, others a mosque at the entrance.

TABRISI:18:21-24/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:21-24/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:21-24/r1.claim: ʿAthara means to come upon something; aʿthara means to reveal it, and an ʿāthūr is a pit dug to catch a lion, hence a person caught in trouble is said to have fallen into one.

TABRISI:18:21-24/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:21-24/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:21-24/r3.claim: The time phrase idh yatanaazaʿūn may attach to ‘We revealed them’ or to ‘so they would know.’

TABRISI:18:21/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:21/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:21/r1.claim: The proposed ‘waaw of eight’ in the opening of 18:21 is an unfamiliar grammatical category unknown to grammarians; the argument from Paradise's eight gates is unsound.

TABRISI:18:21/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:21/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:21/r2.claim: The exegetes recount that the ruler who sealed the youths in the cave expected them to die there, while two believers recorded their names, lineage, and story on lead and hid the record in a copper chest in the wall.

TABRISI:18:21/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:21/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TABRISI:18:21/r3.claim: The later righteous ruler who governed the region is called Nadlis; another transmitted form of his name is Bandusis.

TABRISI:18:21/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:21/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:21/r4.claim: After generations passed, people divided over resurrection; the righteous king prayed for a sign, and God caused the cave entrance structure to be dismantled, awakened the youths, and exposed their story when one went to seek food.

TABRISI:18:21/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:21/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:21/r5.claim: The youths' long sleep while alive and their awakening demonstrate that the one who can preserve and awaken them can also cause death and resurrection.

TABRISI:18:21/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:21/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:21/r6.claim: The dispute about resurrection included those who denied it, those who accepted resurrection of souls alone, and those who affirmed resurrection of both souls and bodies.

TABRISI:18:21/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:21/r7.speaker: عكرمة
TABRISI:18:21/r7.claim: The phrase about disputing their affair is an idiom for what people did in their matter, as in the cited Arabic expression.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p122#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p122#3/r1.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p122#3/r1.claim: أعثرنا means we made them known and exposed them; the root refers to stumbling on something and inspecting it, as in the idiom of discovering a fault.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p122#3/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p122#3/r10.speaker: ابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p122#3/r10.claim: Another view says the people who converted after seeing the youths proposed the building.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p122#3/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p122#3/r11.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p122#3/r11.claim: Those who prevailed over the matter were the people obeyed, meaning leaders and chiefs.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p122#3/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p122#3/r12.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p122#3/r12.claim: The leaders who prevailed were the king and his believing companions.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p122#3/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p122#3/r13.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p122#3/r13.claim: He reports that the king built a church over them.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p122#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p122#3/r2.speaker: الأكثرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p122#3/r2.claim: The people of the town, disputing resurrection, were shown the youths so they would know God's promise of resurrection and recompense is true and the Hour certain.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p122#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p122#3/r3.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p122#3/r3.claim: Alternatively, God raised the cave companions so they themselves could see the truth of the resurrection promise after learning it.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p122#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p122#3/r4.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p122#3/r4.claim: The phrase about their dispute can mean that they were then disputing, or that they had disputed.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p122#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p122#3/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p122#3/r5.claim: One account says believers wanted a mosque over them because they shared their faith, while polytheists proposed a building because the youths shared their custom.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p122#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p122#3/r6.speaker: عكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p122#3/r6.claim: Another account says they disputed bodily resurrection versus resurrection of souls alone; the youths' raising demonstrated both body and soul are raised.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p122#3/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p122#3/r7.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p122#3/r7.claim: A third view says they disputed what should be done with the youths.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p122#3/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p122#3/r8.speaker: الثعلبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p122#3/r8.claim: Two further reported disputes concerned the length of the youths' stay and their number.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p122#3/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p122#3/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p122#3/r9.claim: One view says the polytheists proposed a building over the youths to hide them from people.

RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r1.claim: After the townspeople saw them, God may have returned the youths to the cave and caused their death; people then disagreed whether they slept again or had now died.

RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r2.claim: Some proposed sealing the cave so no one could enter, while others proposed building a mosque; this second proposal suggests they knew God, worship, and prayer.

RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r3.claim: Another account says unbelievers claimed the sleepers followed their religion and wanted a monument, while Muslims said they followed theirs and proposed a mosque.

RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r4.claim: Other reported disputes concerned how long the youths stayed and their number and names.

RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r5.claim: “Their Lord knows best” may be the disputants' admission after failing to establish their names, circumstances, or duration, or it may be God's own correction of their speculation.

RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r6.claim: Those who prevailed over the matter are variously identified as the Muslim king, the sleepers' relatives, or the town's leaders.

RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p89#2/r7.claim: They proposed a mosque where people could worship God and preserve the youths' traces.

RAZI-FULL:v21p89/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p89/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p89/r1.claim: As with their guidance and awakening, God made others discover their state because it carried evident lessons; athartu means to discover or learn something, from stumbling upon it and then recognizing it.

RAZI-FULL:v21p89/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p89/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p89/r2.claim: One explanation says their unusually long hair and nails and altered facial appearance revealed that an extraordinary length of time had passed.

RAZI-FULL:v21p89/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p89/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p89/r3.claim: Another account says the emissary's old coins were recognized by a seller as long obsolete; the king learned the man had fled Daqyānūs the day before and concluded God had revived him.

RAZI-FULL:v21p89/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p89/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p89/r4.claim: God revealed the youths so people would know His promise of resurrection is true; their awakening after a long sleep demonstrates bodily resurrection.

RAZI-FULL:v21p89/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p89/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p89/r5.claim: One account says the king denied resurrection but was fair-minded; another says people disputed whether body and soul or only the soul would be raised, and the king prayed for a sign that settled the issue.

RAZI-FULL:v21p89/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p89/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p89/r6.claim: The phrase “while they were disputing among themselves” attaches to God making the people discover the youths, at the time of their dispute.

RAZI-FULL:v21p89/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p89/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p89/r7.claim: Their dispute may have concerned resurrection: believers used God's preservation of the bodies for 309 years as proof that He can raise bodies after death.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#2/r1.speaker: النبي ﷺ
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#2/r1.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas curses women who frequently visit graves and those who make mosques and lamps over them; al-Tirmidhi grades it hasan.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#2/r2.speaker: النبي ﷺ
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#2/r2.claim: A report from Aisha says churches with images were built over righteous men's graves; the Prophet calls such builders the worst of creation, and jurists forbid mosques at prophets' and scholars' graves.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#2/r3.speaker: النبي ﷺ
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#2/r3.claim: The Prophet forbids praying toward graves or sitting on them; Qurtubi explains that using a grave as a qibla can lead to worship of its occupant.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#2/r4.speaker: النبي ﷺ
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#2/r4.claim: A report warns of God's severe anger against people who take prophets' and righteous people's graves as mosques, closing a path toward grave worship.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#2/r5.speaker: النبي ﷺ
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#2/r5.claim: Aisha and Ibn Abbas report that during his final illness the Prophet cursed Jews and Christians for making prophets' graves into mosques.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#2/r6.speaker: النبي ﷺ
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#2/r6.claim: Jabir reports prohibitions on plastering graves, sitting on them, building on them, writing on them, and walking over them; al-Tirmidhi grades a version hasan sahih.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#2/r7.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#2/r7.claim: Ali says the Prophet ordered him to erase every image and level every raised grave; scholars infer that prominent mounds must be removed.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#2/r8.speaker: الجمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#2/r8.claim: The majority interpret the commanded leveling as removing excess height, while retaining a recognizable, respected grave mound; Malik describes this for the Prophet and his Companions.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#3/r1.claim: Large, ornate grave structures that imitate pre-Islamic glorification should be demolished; the apparent prohibition and use of worldly adornment at the afterlife's first station make them unlawful.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#3/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#3/r10.claim: Al-Qurtubi explains felt lining beneath the Prophet as suited to Medina's salty ground; Shaqran reported placing it there, and al-Tirmidhi grades the report hasan sahih gharib.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#3/r2.claim: Tasnīm is a grave mound about a handspan high, named from a camel's hump, and it is sprinkled with water to prevent wind scattering it.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#3/r3.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#3/r3.claim: Al-Shafiʿi permits coating a grave with mud; Abu Hanifa forbids plaster, mud coating, and a structure above it.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#3/r4.claim: Stones may mark a grave; a report says Fatima visited Hamza's grave weekly and marked it with a stone.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#3/r5.claim: Burial in a coffin is permissible, especially in loose soil; reports describe stone coffins for Daniel and a glass coffin for Joseph until Moses recovered him.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#3/r6.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#3/r6.claim: On his deathbed, Saʿd asked for a lateral niche and upright bricks as used for the Prophet; a lahd is a side chamber in firm earth, preferred by Malik and Abu Hanifa, while al-Shafiʿi prefers a trench.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#3/r7.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#3/r7.claim: Al-Shafiʿi permits bricks in a lahd as a kind of stone; Abu Hanifa and his companions dislike them as building material unsuited to a grave, though another view objects because fire touched the brick.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#3/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#3/r8.claim: Clay bricks and reeds are recommended; a bundle of reeds was reportedly placed on the Prophet's grave.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#3/r9.speaker: أبو بكر محمد بن الفضل
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21#3/r9.claim: The Hanafi jurist permits coffins where soil is loose, even iron ones, with earth beneath the deceased and light bricks at the sides to resemble a lahd.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:21/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21/r1.claim: Aʿtharna means God revealed and brought them to light; the verb is the causative form of ʿathara, originally stumbling with the foot.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:21/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21/r10.claim: Taking graves as mosques, praying at them, and building over them is forbidden by the Prophetic teaching cited next.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:21/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21/r2.claim: After Daqyanus died, a righteous king's town disputed bodily resurrection: some said only souls return, while others held that body and soul rise together.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:21/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21/r3.claim: The puzzled king prayed in ascetic clothing on ashes; a youth's old coin exposed the cave youths, and he recognized them as a sign answering his prayer.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:21/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21/r4.claim: The king and townspeople learned from the youths that the community was Muslim; after they returned to the cave, most reports say they died a true death.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:21/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21/r5.claim: Their discovery restored doubters to certainty that the promised resurrection and the Hour are real, including resurrection of bodies.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:21/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21/r6.claim: When people disputed what to do, one account has the king propose a building and those aligned with the youths choose a mosque; another has Muslims prevail over a church or guesthouse proposal.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:21/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21/r7.claim: Other accounts say some wanted to cover and conceal the cave, or that God hid it from public view so the king proposed a marker building.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:21/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21/r8.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21/r8.claim: Ibn Umar says God obscured the youths from people, which explains the proposal to build a sign over the site.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:21/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:21/r9.claim: A dream report says one youth objected to being buried in a gold chest: they were created from earth and should return to it.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:21/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:21/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:21/r1.claim: The awakening after centuries teaches that resurrection is true and possible: God preserved bodies while withholding souls, then returned the souls.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:21/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:21/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:21/r2.claim: The disputants differed whether resurrection restores souls alone or both souls and bodies.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:21/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:21/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:21/r3.claim: They may also have disputed whether the youths had died again or merely returned to sleep.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:21/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:21/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:21/r4.claim: Another dispute was whether to build a public structure over them or a mosque for prayer.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:21/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:21/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:21/r5.claim: Their story confirms the promise of resurrection; the verse links it to a mosque being built over them by those who prevailed.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:21/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:21/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:21/r6.claim: Their Lord knows best may be God's rebuke to arguers, a contemporary comment, or a statement by later disputants; it may also defer their identity to God after failed speculation.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:21/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:21/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:21/r7.claim: In one account, a coin bearing Daqyanus's name led the city to suspect treasure; a Christian monotheist king heard the story, met the youths, and buried them in a mosque after they returned to sleep and died.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:21/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:21/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:21/r8.claim: Another account says the messenger went in first to spare the others from fright, became unable to find the entrance, and a structure and mosque were built above it.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p8#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p8#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p8#2/r1.claim: God disclosed them just as He had put them to sleep and awakened them, each act serving a wise purpose.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p8#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p8#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p8#2/r2.claim: Their case proves God's promise of resurrection: their sleep and awakening resemble death followed by being raised.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p8#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p8#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p8#2/r3.claim: The townspeople were disputing the nature of resurrection, with some affirming souls alone and others bodies with souls; the sleepers' return settled the dispute.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p8#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p8#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p8#2/r4.claim: One proposal was to build over the cave entrance to keep people from approaching the sleepers' remains, as the Prophet's grave was protected by an enclosure.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p8#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p8#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p8#2/r5.claim: “Their Lord knows them best” may be the disputants' conclusion after failing to establish their lineage, circumstances, or duration, or God's rebuke to speculators.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p8#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p8#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p8#2/r6.claim: The people who prevailed were Muslims and their ruler; they chose a mosque at the cave entrance where Muslims could pray and seek blessing.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p8#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p8#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p8#2/r7.claim: The account says Daqyanus compelled youths to worship idols; they fled with a dog, which God enabled to speak and volunteer as their guard.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p8#2/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p8#2/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p8#2/r8.claim: In the fuller account, a believing king prayed for proof of resurrection, a shepherd opened the cave, and the envoy's old coin exposed the sleepers' story.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p8#2/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p8#2/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p8#2/r9.claim: The city praised God at the sign; after the youths died, the king replaced gold coffins they disliked with teak and built a mosque at the entrance.

QASHANI:18:21-22#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:21-22#2/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:21-22#2/r1.claim: The people with authority over the companions propose a mosque for prayer, seeking blessing through them and their place.

QASHANI:18:21-22#2/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:21-22#2/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:21-22#2/r8.claim: The inward discovery means divine unveiling to realized people that the self survives bodily destruction; the dispute is the faculties’ struggle to control the body in which they will be raised.

QASHANI:18:21-22#2/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:21-22#2/r9.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:21-22#2/r9.claim: The building represents the resurrected body; dominant faculties are its builders, and the mosque signifies animal, natural, and psychic powers submitting within it.

QASHANI:18:21-22/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:21-22/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:21-22/r1.claim: The sleepers’ discovery mirrors resurrection: it reveals prepared souls who can receive guidance and recognize bodily resurrection and recompense.

QASHANI:18:21-22/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:21-22/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:21-22/r2.claim: One unnamed party says resurrection concerns only immaterial spirits, not bodies.

QASHANI:18:21-22/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:21-22/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:21-22/r3.claim: Another party says resurrection joins spirits and bodies; al-Qāshānī endorses this embodied resurrection as the truth.

QASHANI:18:21-22/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:21-22/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:21-22/r4.claim: The proposed building resembles lodges, shrines, and visiting places erected over perfected prophets and saints such as Abraham and Muhammad.

QASHANI:18:21-22/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:21-22/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:21-22/r5.claim: The followers say God knows the saints best because their rank exceeds other people’s knowledge; they are monotheists annihilated in and realized through God.

QASHANI:18:21-22/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:21-22/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:21-22/r6.claim: A divine saying supports the saints’ hiddenness: only God knows His friends.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p157/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p157/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p157/r10.claim: ʿAthara ʿalā al-amr means to discover it, while aʿtharanī means another person showed it to me; the object of أعثرنا is omitted and understood as the people of the town.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p157/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p157/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p157/r9.claim: The narrative compresses the dispatch, food search, tactful return, and lack of detection before God makes the townspeople discover the youths; fuller details in later accounts are not asserted as certain.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158#2/r1.claim: One group reportedly wanted to seal the cave over the youths; the dominant group said to build a mosque and did so.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158#2/r2.claim: Another report says unbelievers sought a church or pagan sanctuary, believers resisted, and the believers built a mosque over them.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158#2/r3.speaker: الحسن وعيسى الثقفي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158#2/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan and ʿĪsā al-Thaqafī read غلبوا with passive vowels; on this reading, the party favoring the mosque wanted nothing built over or brought near the site.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158#2/r4.claim: A further report says believers first wanted the cave left unsealed; once construction prevailed, they proposed that it be a mosque, and it was.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158#2/r5.speaker: ابن عمر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says God concealed the youths’ situation from people, prompting the proposal to build a marker.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158/r1.speaker: الطبري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī takes the subject of ليعلموا to be the townspeople whom God caused to discover the youths.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158/r2.claim: The promise of God is resurrection: the youths’ sleep and awakening after a long interval resemble death and being raised; the Hour and its recompense are certain.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158/r3.claim: A reported background says townspeople doubted bodily resurrection; their king, unable to answer, wore rough garments, sat in ashes, and prayed for proof. The youths’ awakening convinced the people and restored doubters’ certainty.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158/r4.claim: إذ may depend on أعثرنا or ليعلموا; another view takes ليعلموا as the youths, with their case proving bodily resurrection, and إذ then begins the townspeople’s dispute over a building or mosque.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158/r5.claim: Another interpretation says the dispute was whether the youths were dead or alive when discovered.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158/r6.claim: A report says the king and townspeople went with Tamlikha to the cave; after greeting the king and returning to their beds, the youths died, and the king made coffins first of gold, then of teak after seeing their dislike of gold in a dream, and built at the entrance.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158/r7.claim: ربهم أعلم بهم most naturally belongs to the disputants, who exchanged claims about lineage, circumstances, and duration before conceding that God knew best.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158/r8.claim: Alternatively, ربهم أعلم بهم may be a divine reply rebuking speculators among the current disputants or the People of Scripture who debated the Prophet.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158/r9.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p158/r9.claim: Qatāda says those who prevailed over the matter were the rulers.

SAMIN-DURR:18:21/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:21/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:21/r1.claim: أعثرنا means revealed or made them discover, paralleling their sleep and awakening; ليعلموا attaches to it.

SAMIN-DURR:18:21/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:21/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:21/r2.claim: The pronoun may refer to the omitted object الناس or to the cave companions themselves.

SAMIN-DURR:18:21/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:21/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:21/r3.claim: إذ يتنازعون may attach to أعثرنا, ليعلموا, the sense of حق, or وعد where temporal adjuncts may extend broadly.

SAMIN-DURR:18:21/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:21/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:21/r4.claim: Grammarians restricting such attachments reject placing it before the relative clause is complete.

SAMIN-DURR:18:21/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:21/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:21/r5.claim: بنيانا may be a direct object meaning a building or a مصدر.

SAMIN-DURR:18:21/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:21/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:21/r6.claim: ربهم أعلم بهم may be God's speech or the disputants' speech.

SAMIN-DURR:18:21/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:21/r7.speaker: عيسى الثقفي والحسن
SAMIN-DURR:18:21/r7.claim: They read غلبوا with damma on غين and kasra on لام.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p146/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p146/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p146/r1.claim: Earlier people of that age disputed resurrection and the Hour; more than one early authority is said to report this doubt.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p146/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p146/r2.speaker: عكرمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p146/r2.claim: A group held that souls would be raised but bodies would not; God made the Sleepers a proof and sign against that view.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p146/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p146/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p146/r3.claim: When one sleeper went to buy food in the city he found its people and landmarks transformed; his old coinage drew suspicion, and he said he remembered the city under Diocletian the previous evening.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p146/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p146/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p146/r4.claim: An unnamed poet is cited to contrast familiar dwellings with inhabitants changed beyond recognition.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p146/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p146/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p146/r5.claim: One account says the returning sleeper asked to enter first to tell his companions, but people did not know how he disappeared and God concealed what happened.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p146/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p146/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p146/r6.claim: Another account says the people entered, and the Muslim ruler Tydosis greeted and embraced the sleepers; they spoke with him, returned to their resting places, and God caused them to die.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, campaigning with Habib ibn Maslama in Byzantine territory, saw bones in a cave; he said the Sleepers' bones had decayed after more than three hundred years. Ibn Jarir transmits it.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147/r2.claim: As God first caused the Sleepers to lie down and then woke them in their recognizable forms, He exposed them to that generation as proof of resurrection for believers and deniers alike.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147/r3.claim: The suggestion to build over them means sealing the cave entrance and leaving them as they were.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147/r4.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147/r4.claim: Two views identify those who proposed building a mosque: the believers among them, or the polytheists; Ibn Kathir leaves the matter to God.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147/r5.claim: The proposal came from people with authority, but whether it deserves praise is doubtful in light of the Prophet's warning against turning prophets' and righteous people's graves into mosques.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147/r6.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147/r6.claim: The Prophet cursed Jews and Christians for taking the graves of their prophets and righteous people as mosques, warning against that practice.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147/r7.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p147/r7.claim: When Umar found Daniel's grave in Iraq, he ordered it hidden from people and a scroll found with it, containing prophecies and other material, buried.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p457/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p457/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p457/r3.claim: God's making the sleepers known encompasses strengthening their hearts, concealing them, protecting them from oppressors, and preserving their bodies over time.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p457/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p457/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p457/r4.claim: The preserved bodies and revival after more than three centuries demonstrate bodily resurrection against those who thought only souls would be raised.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p457/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p457/r5.speaker: بعض العارفين
BIQAI-FULL:v4p457/r5.claim: A wise teacher says waking after sleep teaches resurrection after death; the intermediate state is one, though the soul remains attached to the body in sleep.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p457/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p457/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p457/r6.claim: The Hour is beyond doubt, supported by rational evidence and decisive transmitted proofs.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p457/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p457/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p457/r7.claim: The disputants debate whether resurrection is only of souls or includes bodies, and whether the sleepers were righteous or their state was unknown.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p457/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p457/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p457/r8.claim: The party in control proposes a building over them; the author prefers reading the phrase as city leaders or powerful people, whom God made righteous.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p457/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p457/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p457/r9.claim: The author infers the sleepers died again after their discovery, before all details were investigated; their story encourages migration.

DURR-FULL:v5p366/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p366/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p366/r5.claim: At the cave, the youth asked the crowd to wait while he entered first so his companions would not be frightened; he then disappeared, and they could not enter.

DURR-FULL:v5p366/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p366/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p366/r6.claim: Unable to reach the sleepers, the people decided to build a mosque over them and pray there, seeking forgiveness for them.

DURR-FULL:v5p373/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p373/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p373/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas explains أعثرنا عليهم as making them known or discovered.

DURR-FULL:v5p373/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p373/r13.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v5p373/r13.claim: Al-Suddi relates that elders identified the lost youths as those who disappeared under King Decius, with their names recorded on a stone at the city gate.

DURR-FULL:v5p375/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p375/r1.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v5p375/r1.claim: The king found the names on the stone, learned that the youths who had died had been raised, and rejoiced that this proved the dead would be resurrected; he resolved to build a mosque at their site.

DURR-FULL:v5p375/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p375/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p375/r2.claim: Those who prevailed in the dispute and ordered a mosque to be built were rulers or sultans.

DURR-FULL:v5p375/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p375/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v5p375/r3.claim: The king built a church over them and inscribed that its founders were sons of leaders and landowners.

BURSEVI:v5p177#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p177#2/r1.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v5p177#2/r1.claim: His story says Yamlīkhā found the city transformed after roughly three centuries; an old coin bearing Decianus's name led to his arrest as a supposed treasure finder, and people mocked his claim that Decianus summoned him the day before.

BURSEVI:v5p177#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p177#2/r2.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v5p177#2/r2.claim: The townspeople took him to the king; he explained his companions had sent him for food and led them to the cave, where the king and nobles read the tablet and found the youths looking fresh in new clothes.

BURSEVI:v5p178#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p178#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p178#2/r1.claim: Some exegetes attach إذ يتنازعون to an omitted اذكر; the author prefers this because it fits the following فاء and separates the phrase from what precedes.

BURSEVI:v5p178#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p178#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p178#2/r2.claim: The disputants were the people of Tindrous, debating what to do with the site after the youths died again and how to conceal access.

BURSEVI:v5p178#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p178#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p178#2/r3.claim: One group proposed a building over the cave entrance to protect the grave and said God knew the youths, so outsiders need not know their location.

BURSEVI:v5p178#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p178#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p178#2/r4.claim: The Muslims and their king resolved to build a mosque at the cave entrance for prayer and seeking blessing at the youths' place.

BURSEVI:v5p178/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p178/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p178/r1.claim: As with their sleep and awakening, God exposed the youths to display His power and wisdom and strengthen their certainty.

BURSEVI:v5p178/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p178/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p178/r2.claim: Aʿtharna means making people discover them, from the image of stumbling upon something hidden; the cause is named for the knowledge it produces.

BURSEVI:v5p178/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p178/r3.speaker: تهذيب المصادر
BURSEVI:v5p178/r3.claim: The lexicon glosses إعثار as bringing someone upon a thing and اطلاع as bringing someone to hidden knowledge.

BURSEVI:v5p178/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p178/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p178/r4.claim: Discovery convinced people who denied bodily resurrection that God's promise is true: He held the youths' souls while preserving their bodies for centuries, then returned the souls, as He will gather all bodies for judgment.

BURSEVI:v5p178/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p178/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p178/r5.claim: God graciously guided the people through the sign of sleep, proving the truth in a way that served as a messenger's proof for receptive hearts.

BURSEVI:v5p178/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p178/r6.speaker: الإمام الثعلبي
BURSEVI:v5p178/r6.claim: A report says the Prophet wished to see the Cave youths; Gabriel said he would not see them in this world, so he sent Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿAlī, and Abū al-Dardāʾ to invite them to Islam. Solomon's swift mount carried them; the dog first barked then recognized them. The youths awoke, exchanged greetings, accepted Islam, conveyed greetings to Muhammad, and slept again; they will awaken to greet the Mahdī and die before resurrection.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p232#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p232#2/r1.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v15p232#2/r1.claim: A scholar argues that seeing God preserve the youths' souls and bodies for over three hundred years and return their souls proves He can resurrect, judge, and reward the dead.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p232#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p232#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p232#2/r2.claim: Alusi questions whether the episode establishes judgment and recompense; an objection says preserving bodies is unlike reassembling scattered parts, and he finds the reply from intuitive inference worth considering but not decisive.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p232/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p232/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p232/r1.claim: The youths sent one of their number, identified by many as Yamlikha; God caused them to be discovered just as He had put them to sleep and awakened them.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p232/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p232/r2.speaker: العز بن عبد السلام
ALUSI-FULL:v15p232/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbd al-Salam takes the demonstrative to refer specifically to their awakening after the long sleep.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p232/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p232/r3.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v15p232/r3.claim: Raghib gives the original meaning of ʿathara as falling face-first and cites proverbs about a generous horse rarely stumbling and the safe well-trodden road.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p232/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p232/r4.speaker: المطرزي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p232/r4.claim: Al-Mutarrizi explains discovery as a metaphor from stumbling: a fallen person looks at where he fell, so the word came to mean finding out, by a familiar causal relation.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p232/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p232/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p232/r5.claim: The first object of aʿtharnā is omitted to make it general: God let people discover the youths.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p232/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p232/r6.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v15p232/r6.claim: Abu Hayyan identifies the people who learned as the townspeople who saw the youths' extraordinary condition; God's promise means the resurrection promise or what He promised, namely resurrection, is true and certain.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p232/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p232/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p232/r7.claim: The Hour is the time when all creatures are raised for judgment and recompense; witnessing the youths' extraordinary death-like sleep and awakening defeats reliance on improbability as a reason to doubt it.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p233/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p233/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p233/r1.claim: Alusi prefers explaining the inference from the youths' preserved bodies, suspended senses, and restoration after centuries: an event as extraordinary as resurrection removes the doubt that arises from finding resurrection improbable.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p233/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p233/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p233/r2.claim: The event directly establishes resurrection's possibility, not certainty that it will happen; certainty of fulfillment comes from the truthful report, while the event supplies a final part of the proof for those who heard it.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p233/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p233/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p233/r3.claim: Another interpretation makes God's promise cover all He promised and the Hour a specification after that general statement; Alusi accepts it as a possible reading but disputes calling it the obvious one.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p233/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p233/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p233/r4.claim: The temporal phrase idh yatanaazaʿun most naturally modifies aʿtharnā, placed first to emphasize the purpose; Abu Hayyan and Abu al-Baqa also attach it to liyaʿlamu, though Alusi raises objections.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p233/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p233/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p233/r5.claim: Tanaazuʿ originally means pulling against one another and figuratively means disputing; it takes a direct object in its literal sense but fi with the sense of quarrel.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p233/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p233/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p233/r6.claim: The dispute is about resurrection: people differed between affirming it, denying it, raising souls alone, or raising both souls and bodies, the last being the Muslim doctrine.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p233/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p233/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p233/r7.claim: A narrative says a later believing king, faced with disagreement over resurrection, prayed for a sign; a shepherd opened the cave, the youths awoke, their old coins exposed their story, and after meeting the king they died, were placed in wooden coffins, and a mosque was built.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p234/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p234/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p234/r1.claim: An alternative report says the king matched the youth's names to an old tablet, then the youth entered first to spare his companions fear; God took their souls and obscured their traces, and the townspeople built a mosque after trusting the youth's account.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p234/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p234/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p234/r2.claim: Another interpretation makes their affair the story of their former ordeal under the tyrant, which people had heard as legend without knowing whether the youths survived.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p234/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p234/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p234/r3.claim: On either interpretation, the fa before build is an abbreviated transition: the purpose of discovery was achieved, the youths died, and the people then proposed a structure at the cave entrance.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p234/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p234/r4.speaker: الراغب، أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v15p234/r4.claim: Bunyanan is parsed either as a singular noun with no plural, a plural of bunyana, or a cognate accusative; the builders sought to protect the youths' resting place from intrusion.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p235/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p235/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p235/r1.claim: Rabbuhum aʿlam bihim may be the finders submitting knowledge of lineage, condition, and duration to God, or God's rebuke to those speculating, including the finders or the People of the Book in the Prophet's time.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p235/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p235/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p235/r2.claim: Some assign amrahum to the youths and read the dispute as what to do after their death, how to honor them, or uncertainty whether they had died or merely slept again.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p235/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p235/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v15p235/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari offers further options: amrahum may concern the finders' religion and resurrection, the people's discussion of the cave youths' story, or plans to conceal the youths' location after death.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p235/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p235/r4.speaker: صاحب الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v15p235/r4.claim: The author of al-Kashf distinguishes the conjunction: the fa is explanatory in one account and consecutive in the others, including when people stop discussing the story and turn to the practical matter of building.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p235/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p235/r5.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v15p235/r5.claim: Abu Hayyan allows the pronoun in liyaʿlamu to refer to the youths, with their discovery increasing their knowledge; the dispute then begins a new account about the townspeople and their building plans.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p235/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p235/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p235/r6.claim: Alusi says this reading is not far-fetched if one sets aside external reports, though he knows of no commentator who takes all the pronouns as referring to the youths and idh as modifying discovery.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p236#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p236#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p236#2/r1.claim: A report says the first group were unbelievers seeking a church or pagan sanctuary, while believers opposed them and built a mosque; another report says the king built a church with an inscription, suggesting mosque here names the Christian community's place of worship.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p236#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p236#2/r2.speaker: السدي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p236#2/r2.claim: Al-Suddi reports that the king planned a mosque beside the righteous youths where he could worship God until death.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p236#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p236#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v15p236#2/r3.claim: Hasan says the mosque was for the youths to pray in upon waking; this assumes they remained asleep, a view extended by some to say they await the Mahdi, which Alusi dismisses as fables.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p236#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p236#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p236#2/r4.claim: If the first group were unbelievers, not every finder shared the resurrection lesson; they may have wished to seal the cave because they did not know the youths had slept and awakened.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p236#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p236#2/r5.speaker: الحسن، عيسى الثقفي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p236#2/r5.claim: They read ghulibū in the passive: believing finders who opposed construction were overpowered and yielded that, if anything were built, it should be a mosque.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p236#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p236#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p236#2/r6.claim: Alusi rejects using the verse to permit building mosques over righteous graves or praying there, despite al-Khafaji's claim; he cites multiple prophetic reports cursing grave-visitors who make mosques and lamps at graves and those who turn prophets' graves into mosques.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p236#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p236#2/r7.speaker: رسول الله
ALUSI-FULL:v15p236#2/r7.claim: Reports from Ibn Abbas, Aisha, Abu Hurayra, and others condemn turning prophets' graves into mosques; another says people who build over a righteous person's grave and place images there are among the worst at the Resurrection.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p236#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p236#2/r8.speaker: رسول الله
ALUSI-FULL:v15p236#2/r8.claim: Other reports call grave-mosque makers among the worst people and say God cursed earlier Israelites for making graves into mosques.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p236/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p236/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p236/r1.claim: Alusi considers it remote that rabbuhum aʿlam is God's speech rebuking the disputants, and very remote to assign all pronouns to the youths; its apparent sense is the finders' response to uncertainty over life and death.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p236/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p236/r2.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p236/r2.claim: Qatada, in reports from ʿAbd al-Razzaq and Ibn Abi Hatim, identifies those who prevailed as the rulers; their first-person oath to build suits people with authority.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p236/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p236/r3.speaker: author
